text:
maria: quick update from the kernel+batch-sweep I ran last night across A10/T4/L4/A100/H100. posting top-level observations first, then small config proposal.

maria: TL;DR: H100/A100 still robust at high max_tokens_per_batch, but L4 and A10 hit kernel fallback paths and KV-fragmentation regressions when we pushed tokens too high. T4 sits in the middle and is sensitive to prefix lengths.

devon: can you paste the config you used for the sweep? especially queue policy + batching window.

maria: sure — this is the driver we used (simplified):
```
queue_policy:
  bucket_ms: 12
  max_wait_ms: 40
  max_batch_tokens_by_gpu:
    A10: 28000
    T4: 14000
    L4: 9000
    A100: 36000
    H100: 52000
kv_cache:
  prefetch_prefix_pct: 0.18
  eviction_tolerance: 0.03
```

bench-bot: run 2026-03-10T03:12Z complete — per-gpu latency p95 and kernel-fallback counts attached in run metadata (see run 2026-03-10/slot-3).

kevin: where are the kernel-fallback counts highest? L4?

maria: highest on L4 and A10 for long sequences (>=2k tokens). fallback churn increases 3x when max_batch_tokens > ~10k on L4 and >24k on A10. A100/H100 show near-zero fallback until we exceed 40k/48k respectively.

alex: interesting. any KV-fragmentation numbers? that usually kills throughput on multi-model mixes.

maria: yes — KV-frag events per minute (normalized): L4: 18, A10: 12, T4: 7, A100: 2, H100: 1. When KV-frag spikes, effective tokens/sec drops ~22%.

devon: sounds like we should tighten max_tokens_per_batch for L4 and A10 in the short term and add a softcap + graceful degrade to avoid sudden fallbacks. propose numbers?

kevin: propose we switch to a two-tier policy: hard ceiling + soft target. soft target = conservative number we try to form; hard ceiling = fail-safe. also reduce bucket_ms on L4 to reduce aggregation skew.

maria: my suggested numbers from the sweep:
- L4: soft_target=8000, hard_ceiling=11000, bucket_ms=8
- T4: soft_target=12000, hard_ceiling=16000, bucket_ms=10
- A10: soft_target=22000, hard_ceiling=30000, bucket_ms=12
- A100: soft_target=32000, hard_ceiling=42000, bucket_ms=14
- H100: soft_target=44000, hard_ceiling=60000, bucket_ms=16

alex: that soft/hard separation feels sane. can we wire an automatic rollback trigger if kernel fallback rate > 1/min for 2m?

ops: yes — we can add an alert + automated policy that reduces soft_target by 20% and notifies the channel. ops will own the runbook.

devon: one more nuance — on mixes with heavy prefix reuse the KV-cache prefetch percentage mattered. with prefetch=0.18 we saw more KV-frag on L4. lowering to 0.12 cut frag events ~30% but slightly increased cold token latency.

maria: tradeoff seems worth it for L4 and A10. I'll push a staged change: adjust L4/A10 prefetch to 0.12, apply the soft/hard targets above, and reduce bucket_ms for L4. then run the same sweep for mixed traffic and short/long sequence mixes.

bench-bot: scheduled sweep job 4456789012-2 queued (estimated 3h). will post artifact link when done.

kevin: nice. for rollout plan: stage 1 (1% traffic, 2h), stage 2 (25% 6h), stage 3 (100% 24h) with auto-rollback on kernel-fallback > 1/min sustained 2m.

maria: agreed. I'll draft the PR with config + experiment gating. ping me if you want to review the numbers.

devon: will review. thanks maria :thumbsup:

ops: added runbook stub to infra runbooks -> batch-policy-rollback. link: https://internal/runbooks/batch-policy-rollback

maria: leaving this thread open for bench-bot results. thanks all.
